reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises. The claims about the initial microstructure, the effect of the specific annealing treatment on CrMnFeCoNi, the mechanistic link between grain refinement and oxidation/spallation resistance, and the role of cooling rate are all presented without reference to prior experimental or theoretical work.
premises: As-deposited CrMnFeCoNi HEA bond coats have a coarse-grained structure with porosity and microcracks
Annealing at ~900°C for 1–2 hours induces recrystallization and grain refinement in this alloy
Grain refinement reduces stress concentration sites and enhances protective oxide formation via improved diffusion paths
Refined microstructure improves oxidation resistance and reduces spallation during thermal cycling
Optimized cooling rate maintains beneficial residual stresses and prevents grain coarsening
